sourcesRead.title: Evaluating Text Generation Quality Using Spectral Distances of Surprisal (Liu, Li, Xu, Wang, Yuan, Yang; Findings of EMNLP 2025)
Decoding Decoded: Understanding Hyperparameter Effects in Open-Ended Text Generation (Garces Arias, Li, Heumann, Assenmacher)

claims.claim: Liu and colleagues evaluate generated text by the spectrum of its surprisal over position, the dynamic pattern of how surprisal rises and falls through a text, rather than by a static likelihood score.
claims.source: Liu, Li, Xu, Wang, Yuan, Yang, 'Evaluating Text Generation Quality Using Spectral Distances of Surprisal', Findings of EMNLP 2025
claims.modelEra: Qwen2 family 1.5B to 72B and models up to 70B, observation 2025; registers measured: Wikipedia-English, BBC-News, WritingPrompts stories, plus three Chinese corpora

claims.claim: Liu and colleagues report that in their smoothed surprisal spectra the larger models produce a spectrum closer to the human one than the smaller models do.
claims.source: Liu, Li, Xu, Wang, Yuan, Yang, Findings of EMNLP 2025
claims.modelEra: Qwen2 1.5B, 7B and 72B, 2025; registers measured: Wikipedia, news and story continuations in English and Chinese

claims.claim: Liu and colleagues state that the earlier Fourier-of-surprisal work's conclusions about model scaling and sampling methods, having been developed on GPT-2 output, need not hold for current large language models.
claims.source: Liu, Li, Xu, Wang, Yuan, Yang, Findings of EMNLP 2025
claims.quote: and sampling methods does not necessarily apply
claims.modelEra: comment on GPT-2-era findings from a 2025 vantage; registers measured in the new study: Wikipedia, news, stories

claims.claim: Liu and colleagues report that texts generated with top-p at 0.95 and top-k at 40 score better on their surprisal-spectrum metric than those from the simpler sampling settings they compare.
claims.source: Liu, Li, Xu, Wang, Yuan, Yang, Findings of EMNLP 2025
claims.quote: with more advanced sampling method (e.g., top-p
claims.page: Section 4.2, 'Comparison with sampling methods' (details in Appendix B.1)
claims.confidenceReason: the body states the direction and defers the numbers to Appendix B.1, which was not read
claims.modelEra: Qwen2 and Llama3 family models, 2025; registers measured: Wikipedia, news, stories

claims.claim: Garces Arias and colleagues conclude from 2.2 million generated continuations that the best decoding hyperparameters differ from model to model and task to task, with no single configuration best everywhere.
claims.source: Garces Arias, Li, Heumann, Assenmacher, 'Decoding Decoded', arXiv:2410.06097v2 (2024)
claims.quote: that optimal configurations vary across models
claims.modelEra: GPT2-XL, Mistral 7B v0.3, Llama3 8B, Falcon2 11B, Qwen2, observation late 2024; registers measured: book, wikinews and wikitext continuations

claims.claim: Garces Arias and colleagues report that in their comparison larger models showed no clear advantage over smaller ones, with GPT2-XL at 1.5B parameters sometimes scoring above Llama3 at 8B.
claims.source: Garces Arias, Li, Heumann, Assenmacher, arXiv:2410.06097v2 (2024)
claims.quote: Larger models do not show a clear
claims.page: Section 5 results discussion; the top-five table of decoding methods per dataset
claims.modelEra: GPT2-XL 1.5B, Llama3 8B, Falcon2 11B, Qwen2, Mistral 7B v0.3, late 2024; registers measured: book, wikinews, wikitext

claims.claim: Garces Arias and colleagues report that beam search performed consistently poorly against human references across all their models and beam widths, failing to capture the diversity of human language.
claims.source: Garces Arias, Li, Heumann, Assenmacher, arXiv:2410.06097v2 (2024)
claims.quote: that fail to capture the diversity of human language.
claims.modelEra: GPT2-XL, Mistral 7B v0.3, Llama3 8B, Falcon2 11B, Qwen2, late 2024; registers measured: book, wikinews, wikitext

claims.claim: Garces Arias and colleagues built their decoding comparison on 2.2 million generated text continuations, released publicly, evaluated with automatic metrics alongside human judgments.
claims.source: Garces Arias, Li, Heumann, Assenmacher, arXiv:2410.06097v2 (2024)
claims.modelEra: five open-source model families, late 2024; registers measured: book, wikinews, wikitext
